- When sentiment is high (≥0.75) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +2–4% above recent peak.
- If sentiment is low (≤0.33) and price is trending down, model underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to avoid mean reversion underestimation.
- Model consistently underestimates true outcomes in the 1st–3rd day of a new 30-day horizon; adjust downward by 0.5–2% for early period.
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating 0.5–0.75), model overfits short-term noise; smooth forecast by averaging last 3–5 values before final output.
- If true outcome exceeds forecast by >5% in 3 consecutive days, model is lagging; increase forecast by 1–2% for next period to catch momentum.
